Officer's narrative
Driver 1 was stopped at a red light in the left lane of a city street in Pasadena, Texas, when the rear of the vehicle
was struck by Driver 2, whose vehicle was traveling behind it. Driver 2 stated that he was uanble to stop in time.
Driver 1 reoprted neck pain and was assisted by emergency medical personnel at the scene, where a Passenger
seated in the front right position was also present and confirmed the sequence of events. Responding officers and
nearby residents confirmed that Driver 1 was inside the vehicle at the time of impact, though no independent
witnesses to the collision itself were located. Photographs taken at the scene show damage to the rear bumper, trunk
lid and tail lamp assembly, which is largely consistent with the reported impact. A few older scratches were also noted
on the rear panel, and these may predate this incident. Driver 1 is listed as a named insured on the policy involved.
Whether the reported neck injury resulted from this collision has not yet been determined and will require further
medical review.

- occurrence_support: Do independent sources (witnesses, photos, cameras, the other driver) confirm that the accident happened as described? Allowed: Confirmed, Partially corroborated, Uncorroborated, Contradicted, Suspected staged.
- damage_crash_fit: Does the vehicle damage fit the described impact? Allowed: Strong, Reasonable, Unclear, Inconsistent.
- occupant_presence: Was the claimant really in the vehicle at the time of the crash? Allowed: Verified, Unclear, Added later, Not present.
- occupants_listed: How many people does the police report list in the insured vehicle (Vehicle 1)? The rating is a whole number. Allowed: a whole number.
- prior_damage_evidence: Is there evidence of vehicle damage from before this crash? Allowed: None, Possible, Documented, Material.
- driver_status: Is the driver of the insured vehicle on the policy? Allowed: Listed, Household, Unlisted, Excluded.
